overall_quality.evidence: Hash tables use a variety of methods to handle collisions, including chaining and open addressing. Chaining involves storing collided items in a linked list at the same index. Open addressing, on the other hand, searches for the next available slot in the table. Both methods ensure that each key-value pair can be stored and retrieved efficiently.
